title: KeyProvider with macOS Keychain
description: Spec §6.4 and §6.1. Evaluate @napi-rs/keyring (backend, pinned version, compiled-binary compatibility) before adopting. A KeyProvider port with a Keychain adapter and a test double. It loads the vault key and creates it only when absent, never replacing an existing key. A locked or unavailable keychain fails within a bounded time. `ward setup` itself moved to WCLI-20 on 2026-09-28, because T01 and T02 need the WCLI-6 store.

acceptanceCriteria.text: KeyProvider loads a vault key and creates one only when none exists, refusing to replace an existing key; a missing, locked, unavailable or wrong-length key yields a fixed catalogue error and never causes a key to be generated (the key side of T02)
The Keychain adapter is exercised through a compiled executable built by scripts/build.ts, and it uses the production service name only outside tests
The keyring binding decision (adopt or reject, with reasons) is recorded in the key-custody ADR

Measured and recorded in docs/adr/0001: whether @napi-rs/keyring stores the item in the legacy file-based keychain or the data-protection keychain, using one throwaway item in a test namespace. The developer authorises that real-keychain write when this task starts; no agent or orchestrator can authorise it

Every credential-store call the KeyProvider makes settles within its stated bound (10 s by default), the bound applied is the stated one, and a timed-out or failed existence check is never followed by a write

implementationNotes: Criterion 4 measurement, 2026-09-28. My user authorised one throwaway item plus a cross-build read, asked at task start per the orchestrator's ruling. Setup: @napi-rs/keyring 2.1.0 AsyncEntry, bun 1.3.14 --compile with the WCLI-16 flags, macOS arm64, run from this agent's shell. Service opum.ward.probe-034d79b9, a random synthetic 32-byte value that was never printed. Results: (1) BACKEND: setSecret wrote a class genp item into the LEGACY FILE-BASED login keychain (~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db), visible to 'security find-generic-password' with attributes only. It is not the data-protection keychain. (2) SAME-BUILD read (probe-a, cdhash bfdccdf1...): the value came back with no prompt in about 9 ms. (3) CROSS-BUILD read (probe-b, cdhash 8a2b9acd..., different code identity): refused in 16 ms with 'Platform failure: User interaction is not allowed.' (errSecInteractionNotAllowed), and no prompt was shown. This confirms that the ACL trusts the creating build's cdhash only. In this non-GUI agent shell a foreign build fails fast rather than hanging. The GUI-terminal prompt path is NOT measured here. (4) DELETE from the trusting build returned true, and security then reported not found (exit 44); nothing remains. (5) Binding quirks that contradict its own index.d.ts: getSecret resolves a plain number[] rather than a Uint8Array, and null rather than undefined for an absent item. The adapter must normalize both, and a number[] cannot be zeroed reliably. Provenance: MIT licence, SLSA v1 provenance attestations on both @napi-rs/keyring@2.1.0 and @napi-rs/keyring-darwin-arm64@2.1.0.

Criterion 2 round trip, 2026-09-28. My user authorised it separately from criterion 4. The probe is now committed as test/qualification/keychain-roundtrip.ts. bun test never runs it, and it refuses without WARD_QUALIFY_REAL_KEYCHAIN=1. Built through scripts/build.ts (bun 1.3.14, macOS arm64) from the adapter source at commit 45f5795 and run once from a relocated copy against the real login keychain, service opum.ward.probe-0d9b1f23. Result: loadBefore vault_key_missing; create ok in 17 ms; load ok in 3 ms with bytes matching; secondCreate vault_key_exists; original key intact; deleted true; loadAfterDelete vault_key_missing. security find-generic-password then reported not found (exit 44). No prompt appeared. The committed script's later changes are wording and structure only (opt-in gate, try/finally deletion); it has not been rerun, because the authorisation covered one run. Independent review, two passes by the opum-workflow reviewer, found no critical issues. First pass, 4 highs. H1: the NODE_ENV test guard could be bypassed. It is replaced by a required service name plus a mock of the binding, preloaded from the root and imported first by every test that reaches the store; test-isolation.test.ts enforces that, and the provider test asserts AsyncEntry.name is Refused before constructing anything. H2: the adapter fails closed off darwin, instead of the binding's silent Linux keyutils fallback. H3: criterion 5 is rescoped to the provider bound, and the command-level bound with explicit exit moved to WCLI-20. H4: the double now counts attempts before failure modes apply, with new modes and tests. Mediums fixed: vault_key_write_unconfirmed for indeterminate creates, qualified port and catalogue text, and the reproducible probe. Second pass verified all highs resolved and found 2 new mediums, both fixed: the preload depends on the working directory, and the read-back failure path was untested. Also measured and fixed: NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH loads any module in place of the binding, and NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error or NAPI_RS_WASI_FLAVOR makes the import throw. A module planted in the working directory's node_modules does NOT load under the WASI variables. guard.ts deletes every NAPI_RS_ key, with compiled tests and unguarded controls. The layer check confines native imports, including require, import(), template literals and subpaths, to adapters at the package root. Planted regressions, each reverted afterwards, every one caught: 5 in pass one, 9 in pass two, 6 more after pass two, plus the layer plants. A hard-coded darwin default is equivalent on macOS and is caught only by the Linux CI run. Not done here and recorded: zeroing is best effort. Two zeroing paths are not tested: the owned copy on a failed existence check, and the existing copy. The setTimeout spy patches globals. The check-then-write race against a writer outside Ward cannot be closed in the adapter (see WCLI-20). bun run check passes 178/178.
finalSummary: Added the KeyProvider port and a macOS Keychain adapter over @napi-rs/keyring 2.1.0, pinned exactly. The adapter stores a generic-password item (service opum.ward, account vault-<vaultId>). Every store call is bounded, 10 s by default. Missing, locked, hung or malformed keys raise fixed catalogue codes and never create a key. create refuses to replace any visible item and reports vault_key_write_unconfirmed when its write may have landed. The adapter fails closed off macOS. guard.ts neutralizes the binding's NAPI_RS_ loader variables. Tests cannot reach a real keychain item. Verified: tests against an in-memory double that reproduces the binding's measured shape; compiled-executable tests with controls; two user-authorised real-Keychain runs, one measuring the backend (legacy file-based login keychain, with an ACL that trusts only the creating build) and one a compiled adapter round trip; two independent review passes whose highs and mediums are all fixed; and every planted regression caught. bun run check passes 178/178. Evidence is PR #15 and its CI run. ward setup moved to WCLI-20.
